newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Wages to test Australian bond ranges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Wages to test Australian bond ranges.

text.p: *Australian bonds trawled a fairly narrow trading range during the SYCOM session, finishing slightly lower in the wake of a sell-off in long-dated U.S. Treasuries.
*Final Q1 average weekly earnings at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) likely to provide near term direction.

Australian bond futures contracts trawled a fairly narrow trading range during the SYCOM session, and were somewhat of a sideshow to an impressive 1-1/2 cent rally in the Australian dollar to over US$0.7850.
The June 10-year bond futures contract continued to recoil from this week's SYCOM 92.405 peak, ending after hours trading at 92.285 and down from Wednesday's 92.310 pit close.
Analysts expect initial support at around 92.270 on any further pull-back, while the contract is expected to be restrained at 92.330 resistance ahead of a test of the recent high.

The softer tone reflected weaker long-dated U.S. Treasuries which were weighed down by hedge fund selling and supply concern, while the U.S. short-end remained buoyed by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave policy unchanged on Tuesday.

The key event locally will be the final first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), which will either enliven thoughts of a local policy easing, or finally kill off such ideas. The market will be looking for a weak private sector wage figures of below 1.0 percent to dampen recent concerns over wages growth.

The preliminary AWOTE, which was released earlier this month and did not contain a split between private and public earnings, rose 1.3 percent on the quarter for 4.6 percent year-on-year -- above the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent "line in the sand".

At the same time, the Bureau of Statistics will release first quarter company profits. These are expected to show a fall 2.0 percent after the 8.6 percent rise in the previous quarter, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
